decisive_items: Left testis showed no enhancement in T2, indicating disappearance of the left testis.
No torsion was evident in the sperm vessels;
Pathological examination: Showed hemorrhagic infarction of the left testicular appendage
response.rationale: MRI confirms testicular loss and pathology shows infarction, while torsion is explicitly excluded. Epididymo-orchitis is a plausible precursor but the final diagnosis is testicular infarction.

rejected.why: Pseudomonas infection is a microbiological finding, not the primary diagnosis; it is a contributing cause.
Hemorrhagic infarction is a pathological description, but the MRI indicates testicular loss, making testicular infarction the more accurate clinical diagnosis.
Torsion is explicitly ruled out by the absence of torsion in the sperm vessels.
